value_divergences.where: DataFrameGroupBy sum and mean of a frame in which a float column was added after construction (df['x'] = ..., assign, insert), with the rows already in group order; tests/test_groupby_blocks.py pins Sagebrush's values (pandas gives x sums 0.0 and 0.0 there and means 0.0, Sagebrush sums 1.0 and means 0.25)
value_divergences.reason: the summation path can differ when a float column was added after construction (df['x'] = ..., assign, insert). On ordinary data that's a few ulps; on data with cancellation the sum can differ by the rounding error of the larger terms (e.g. 0 against 1 for [1e100, 1, -1e100, 1]). pandas picks its path per internal block of columns, and an added column is its own block until pandas consolidates; Sagebrush's frame treats a frame's columns of one float dtype as one block, as the constructor and read_csv make them (ruled a documented divergence)

value_divergences.where: DataFrameGroupBy std and median of a frame with float32 columns, one of them added after construction (df['x'] = ..., assign, insert); tests/test_groupby_blocks.py pins Sagebrush's dtypes (pandas gives float32 for a and float64 for the added b there, Sagebrush float64 for both)
value_divergences.reason: pandas computes a float32 column's groupby std and median in float64 and casts the result back to float32 only when every value of the block stays within 5e-4 (absolute) of its float32 cast; an added column is its own block until pandas consolidates. Sagebrush's frame treats a frame's float32 columns as one block, as the constructor and read_csv make them, so one column whose result doesn't fit makes all of them float64. Both compute the result in float64, but pandas can cast one column back to float32 while Sagebrush keeps both in float64. The returned dtypes and the values after rounding can therefore differ
